==Problem==
What is the unit digit of: <cmath>222{,}222-22{,}222-2{,}222-222-22-2?</cmath>
<imath>\textbf{(A) } 0\qquad\textbf{(B) } 2\qquad\textbf{(C) } 4\qquad\textbf{(D) } 8\qquad\textbf{(E) } 10</imath>

==Solution 1==
We can rewrite the expression as <imath>222,222-(22,222+2,222+222+22+2)</imath>. We note that the units digit of <imath>22,222+2,222+222+22+2</imath> is <imath>0</imath> because all the units digits of the five numbers are <imath>2</imath> and <imath>5\cdot2=10</imath>, which has a units digit of <imath>0</imath>. Now, we have something with a units digit of <imath>0</imath> subtracted from <imath>222,222</imath>, and so the units digit of this expression is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 2}</imath>.

==Solution 2==
<cmath>222,222-22,222 = 200,000</cmath>
<cmath>200,000 - 2,222 = 197778</cmath>
<cmath>197778 - 222 = 197556</cmath>
<cmath>197556 - 22 = 197534</cmath>
<cmath>197534 - 2 = 197532</cmath>
So our answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 2}</imath>. (Note that brute forcing takes lots of time and the AMC8 is a timed test)

==Solution 3==
We only care about the units digits. Thus, <imath>2-2</imath> ends in <imath>0</imath>, <imath>0-2</imath> after regrouping(10-2) ends in <imath>8</imath>, <imath>8-2</imath> ends in <imath>6</imath>, <imath>6-2</imath> ends in <imath>4</imath>, and <imath>4-2</imath> ends in <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 2}</imath>.

==Solution 4==
We just take the units digit of each and subtract, adding an extra ten to the first number so we don't get a negative number:
<cmath>(12-2)-(2+2+2+2)=10-8=\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 2}</cmath>

== Solution 5 ==
<cmath>222{,}222-22{,}222-2{,}222-222-22-2\equiv2-2-2-2-2\equiv-8\equiv\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 2}\pmod{10}</cmath>


== Solution 6==

We can ignore the other digits and just do <imath>22-2-2-2-2-2</imath>. Because you are subtracting five <imath>2s</imath> and <imath>2\cdot5 = 10</imath>, you subtract <imath>10</imath> from <imath>22</imath>. This gives us 12, so the last digit is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 2}</imath>.
